newsitem.title: USA: Cohen says U.S. Bosnia pledge hard to keep.
newsitem.headline: Cohen says U.S. Bosnia pledge hard to keep.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Friday he intends to keep U.S. troops in Bosnia until June 1998 as promised but a congressional call for withdrawal by year's end shows it will be difficult.

"It does reflect some sentiment and something that I've expressed to our NATO allies that it's going to very difficult but achieveable to ensure that the United States stays until June of 1998 as NATO has pledged, as the United States has pledged, and we will seek to carry that out," Cohen said.

House members including National Security Committee Chairman Floyd Spence and Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich introduced a bill on Thursday calling for pull out of the U.S. troops from Bosnia by the end of the year.
"It recognises that there is a disagreement on the Hill (Congress) on the part of some members but I think that has been known for some time," Cohen said.
He indicated doubt that opponents have the majorities needed in both the House and Senate for Congress to order the U.S. troops out of Bosnia earlier than pledged.
Cohen has said repeatedly that U.S. troops will leave Bosnia when the present NATO peacekeeping mission ends June 1998 and any further peacekeeping after that should be done by European allies.
But Spence, a South Carolina Republican, said in introducing the year-end pullout bill that President Bill Clinton had assured Congress U.S. troops would leave Bosnia by the end of last year.

Spence also said U.S. peacekeeping costs in Bosnia have grown to an estimated $5.5 billion from a $1.5 billion estimate last year, money that he said must come from an already underfunded defence budget.
But he said he hoped the bill would force a decision by Congress and Clinton on timely withdrawal of U.S. troops from Bosnia.

"The time has come to draw the line and force the administration to face up to the reality that achieving a sustainable peace in Bosnia is unlikely under any realistic time frame," Spence said in a statement. "Under these circumstances, the United States should begin to work immediately toward a policy that permits orderly withdrawal of U.S. ground forces."
